[[Port St. Lucie, Florida]] | awards = }} '''Larry Sanders''' (born November 21, 1988) is a [[basketball]] player for the [[VCU Rams]]. He plays [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] for the [[Virginia Commonwealth University Rams men's basketball|Rams]] and is from [[Fort Pierce, Florida]]. As a junior Sanders averaged 14.4 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks. He has since declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA Draft]]. ==High school career== Sanders wasn't into basketball in the ninth grade. The private school he attended didn't offer sports. Sanders was 6'1" when he transferred to Port St. Lucie. Kareem Rodriguez, the school's basketball coach, spotted Sanders, saw ability and talked him into playing. Sanders was 6'4" after the 10th grade. He was 6'6" after the 11th grade. That's when Rodriguez alerted Tony Pujol, a VCU assistant and friend. Sanders sprouted to 6'9" in his high school senior year. Sanders liked the idea of learning under then VCU head coach [[Anthony Grant]], who previously tutored prominent big men at the [[University of Florida]] as an assistant.[http://www.tcpalm.com/news/2007/dec/25/no-headline-26tsanders/?print=1 Leaps and bounds: Ex-PSL basketball player Larry Sanders growing into role in 1st year at Virginia Commonwealth] Sanders began drawing statewide attention when he helped lead Port St. Lucie to the Class 5A state semifinals his junior season. He averaged 18.9 points and 13 rebounds his senior season, leading Port St. Lucie (20-8) to the District 13-5A championship, and was named first team all-state.[http://www.tcpalm.com/news/2009/nov/07/former-jaguar-star-sanders-drawing-raves/ Former Jaguar star Larry Sanders getting national attention] He committed to the Rams just as some major schools began to show interest. ==College career== For his first two seasons for VCU, Sanders played 2nd star to guard [[Eric Maynor]]. He excelled in that role, utilizing his size and athleticism to disrupt teams defensively. As a sophomore he helped the Rams into the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA Tournament]] against the [[UCLA Bruins]], but lost 65-64 in the first round of the tournament.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=294000023 Maynor misses would-be game winner as UCLA prevails] Sanders went on to have a more prominent role in his junior season after Maynor was drafted into the [[NBA]]. As a junior Sanders averaged 14.4 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks, with 53% field goal percentage, all statistical team highs, on his way to earning the second of his consecutive [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] Defensive Player of the Year awards in 2008-09 and 2009-10.[http://www.vcuramnation.com/2010/04/larry-sanders-declares-for-nba-draft/ Larry Sanders Declares for NBA Draft] Larry Sanders announced in April 2010 after his junior year that he was departing VCU early to enter the [[NBA Draft]].[http://www2.timesdispatch.com/rtd/sports/college/college_basketball/article/VCUB10_20100409-221808/336248/ Rams’ Sanders will enter NBA draft] == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.vcuathletics.com/mbb/0910bios/LarrySanders.php VCU Atletics Bio Page] *[http://www.nbadraft.net/players/larry-sanders NBADraft.net Profile] *[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Larry-Sanders-5148/ DraftExpress.com Profile] *[http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/players/73207 Rivals.com Profile] *[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=36534 ESPN.com Profile] {{DEFAULTSORT:Sanders, Larry}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Basketball players from Florida]]
